results.description: Vexev raised $6 million in new funding to advance FDA 510(k) clearance and United States commercialization of its VxWave robotic tomographic ultrasound platform.
extra_snippets: August 11, 2026—Vexev, an Australia-based medical robotics company, announced it has raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the path to FDA 510(k) clearance and United States commercialization of its VxWave robotic tomographic ultrasound platform, which is designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging. The company advised that the financing round included participation from existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate, and Horizon, together with new investors TreeArc Investment Group, TEN13, Bioshore Ventures, and Alumni Ventures.

The company stated that the new round brings Vexev’s total funding to date to $19 million. According to Vexev, VxWave combines robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition. The platform is being developed for upper limb imaging, with dialysis vascular access as its initial application.

Vexev stated that it intends to expand its autonomous imaging platform beyond dialysis vascular access into additional vascular disease applications like cardiovascular and peripheral artery disease, while building the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions.

results.title: Vexev raises $6M to support robotic ultrasound tech
results.description: Vexev announced today that it raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the progress of its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform.

meta_url.path: › home  › vexev raises $6m to support robotic ultrasound tech

extra_snippets: [Image courtesy of Vexev/U.S. Renal Care]Vexev announced today that it raised $6 million in new funding to accelerate the progress of its robotic tomographic ultrasound platform. Existing investors Blackbird Ventures, Neotribe Ventures, Startmate and Horizon participated in the round.
This round brings Vexev’s total funding to $19 million to date.

Sydney, Australia-based Vexev develops VxWave, an ultrasound platform designed to improve access to standardized vascular imaging. Funding comes on the heels of successful results in a multi-site clinical study shared last fall. VxWave combines robotics, AI and ultrasound imaging to automate vascular ultrasound acquisition. The company is developing the platform for upper limb vascular imaging, targeting dialysis vascular access as an initial application. It integrates advanced robotics, machine learning and ultrasound signal processing.

It also hopes to build the clinical evidence needed to support future AI-enabled decisions. “We believe high-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available,” said John Carroll, co-founder and CEO of Vexev.

results.description: The news: UNSW medical robotics spinout Vexev has raised $8.6 million to accelerate its path to US Food and Drugs Administration clearance and commercialisation of its tomographic ultrasound platform VxWave.
extra_snippets: The news: UNSW medical robotics spinout Vexev has raised $8.6 million to accelerate its path to US Food and Drugs Administration clearance and commercialisation of its tomographic ultrasound platform VxWave. Vexev said this brings the company’s total funding to $27 million.

The company says its VxWave technology “combines robotics, artificial intelligence and ultrasound to define a new category of non-invasive medical imaging”. It is initially being developed for upper-limb vascular imaging for dialysis patients. What they said: “We believe high-quality vascular imaging should be available wherever patients receive care, not only when a specialist is available,” Vexev CEO and co-founder John Carroll said.
